o1.biggest_strength: It picks the right segment with the right seat math and structures the page around the real recruiting jobs to be done: stop email back and forth, spread interviews fairly, route candidates, then handle security.
o1.biggest_mistake: It gets a little too expansive and drifts into strategy and test protocol beyond the copy brief, and the CTA pattern is less disciplined than the brand rule of one action per section.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten to the sharpest sections, keep one primary action more consistently, and make the page feel even more like Cal.com by trimming extra explanation and polishing a few lines.

o2.biggest_strength: It is closest to something I would actually ship: right segment, strong math, good order, direct copy, security surfaced properly, and practical implementation details that help me act on it.
o2.biggest_mistake: The test metric is slightly weaker than it could be because it counts recruiting signups without the first-booking quality filter, which could over-reward lower-intent starts.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Use the stronger qualified-start definition tied to first booking, and sharpen one or two hero lines so the emotional hook lands as hard as the best parts of the page.

reason: Both are good and owner-grade, but 2 is a bit more precise, more publishable, and more immediately usable. 1 has the slightly better success metric, but 2 feels closer to a page I would send to the team to build.
